applicant_utility.summary: Treat this as a tuition discount rather than a stipend: UCL applies the £15,000 to fees first and only pays you directly whatever remains, in three termly instalments, so most overseas fee levels will absorb the whole award. The sole selection criterion is financial need, meaning an excellent academic profile cannot compensate for weak or unverifiable household income evidence. The application is a detailed financial disclosure filed through the International Master's Awards form in Portico, and you must submit one form per programme after your admission application and references are complete.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Overseas-fee students from genuinely low-income households applying to a full-time taught Master's who can document household income.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your fee status shows as Overseas in Portico before the deadline; if the funding form does not appear, contact Admissions rather than waiting
Ensure references are submitted and verified early - an incomplete admission application blocks the scholarship form entirely
Convert household income to GBP for the last completed tax year and gather tax returns, payslips, bank statements or employer letters before mid-May shortlisting
File a separate International Master's Awards form for each programme you want funded
Disclose every other scholarship, loan, family contribution, savings and benefits accurately in the funding questions
common_rejection_risks: Admission application incomplete (references outstanding) at the scholarship deadline, so the funding form never opened
Fee status unconfirmed by UCL Admissions, leaving no accessible funding application
Household income figure that cannot be evidenced when shortlisted
Applying for a distance-learning or part-time programme, which is excluded outright
Assuming the award will cover living costs when most Overseas fees exceed £15,000
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Most of the Overseas tuition fee (typically well above £15,000), the bulk of London living costs, flights, visa fees and the Immigration Health Surcharge, plus non-tuition charges such as bench fees, which UCL states are not normally covered by fee-based funding.
applicant_utility.document_audit: Income evidence must match the figures declared in the form; if you enter zero income you must evidence the alternative income such as state benefits. UCL checks the declared occupation of the main household earner against ISCO-08 categories, so describe it precisely.
alerts: The 2026/27 round closed at 5pm BST on 7 May 2026; UCL expects the next deadline in early May 2027, so start the admission application the preceding autumn
Under UK Government legislation, citizens of Cameroon, Sudan, Myanmar and Afghanistan will be unable to obtain a Study Visa to enter the UK from 26 March 2026
Recipients must inform the UCL Student Funding Office immediately of any other funding awarded, before or after this scholarship
The award can be held alongside other funding, but total funding may lead to adjustment
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Admission application with references completed and fee status confirmed, then the Funding tab in Portico, 'Check and apply', the International Master's Awards financial-need questions, and submit - shortlisting and evidence requests follow in mid-May, results by late June.

applicant_utility.summary: This is UCL's fully funded route for conflict-affected students and it is very small - just up to three awards for 2026/27 - so competition is fierce even among applicants who clearly meet every criterion. It pays full tuition, roughly £20,000 for living costs, visa and Immigration Health Surcharge allowances and one return flight, but it cannot be held alongside any other scholarship, which forces a genuine choice against larger external funding. Documentation, not academic record, drives selection: a valid passport or UN Refugee Travel Document plus provable displacement or serious risk from armed conflict within the last three years.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Students displaced by or at serious risk from armed conflict who hold, or can obtain, refugee status or humanitarian protection outside the UK and want a full-cost route into a UCL taught Master's.
application_readiness_checklist: Secure or renew a passport or UN Refugee Travel Document well before the May-June panel window

Assemble displacement evidence early: UNHCR or host-country refugee status/humanitarian protection, an aid-agency letter, or a signed reference from your residence stating when you arrived and from where
Complete the UCL admission application with references well before the deadline so the funding form unlocks in Portico
Draft the three 200-word answers (passion for your field, contribution to your community, using your UCL learning for change) before opening the form
Calculate household income in GBP for the last completed tax year and be ready to evidence it if shortlisted
common_rejection_risks: No valid passport or UN Refugee Travel Document in place by the selection panel meeting
Already residing in the UK - applications from UK residents are not accepted for this award
Already holding, or studying for, a qualification at or above the level of the course applied for
Applying to a part-time or distance-learning programme
Admission application incomplete because references were not submitted before the scholarship deadline
Answering 'Yes' to Q37 but leaving Q38-43 or the three-answer upload incomplete
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Anything beyond tuition, the approx. £20,000 maintenance and the stated allowances: travel beyond the single return flight, costs for family members (UCL funding supports the student only), and non-tuition charges such as bench fees.
applicant_utility.document_audit: The statement upload must be a Word document or PDF with the three answers at 200 words maximum each, including a word count after each. Displacement evidence may be UNHCR documentation, host-country recognition, an aid-agency letter or a signed residence reference; UCL states it takes into account that displaced applicants may find income evidence harder to obtain.
